Explicitly states the presumption does not cover Article 10.3 quality criteria or other Article 10 data governance duties.
verdict.tone_remark: Professional, neutral, well-structured explanation with no self-reference or hedging.

criterion_remarks: States the plan must be submitted to and approved by the market surveillance authority of the Member State of testing.
Explicitly states registration must use a Union-wide unique single identification number.

verdict.tone_remark: Professional, well-organized third-person exposition with labeled sections and no self-referential hedging.

The answer states the deployer must inform the relevant market surveillance authority.
The answer states the deployer must suspend use of the system.

criterion_remarks: States provider and, where applicable, authorised representative identity and contact details.
Covers intended purpose, accuracy/robustness/cybersecurity, foreseeable risks, explainability, group-specific performance, and input data specs.
States pre-determined changes to the system and its performance from initial conformity assessment.
States human oversight measures under Article 14, including technical measures for interpreting outputs.
States computational/hardware resources, expected lifetime, and maintenance/care measures including software updates.

criterion_remarks: Answer explicitly states codes may be drawn up by individual providers or deployers, by representative organisations, or both.

criterion_remarks: States the provider must appoint, by written mandate, an authorised representative established in the Union.
Explicitly states this must occur before making the system available on the Union market.
Lists all five Article 22(3) tasks: verifying conformity documentation, 10-year record retention, providing information/log access, cooperating with authorities, and registration.
verdict.tone_remark: Professional third-person register with no self-reference, organized by article and obligation though dense in places.
